subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should reply-session initialization conflicts be fixed centrally in the shared session lifecycle, or should webchat and heartbeat get their own retry/requeue paths even if the shared self-heal lands?
rationale: Current source proves both a shared conflict throw and surface-specific terminalization paths; choosing the permanent recovery owner affects session lifecycle safety and whether OpenClaw keeps adding parallel channel retry loops.

options.title: Review shared self-heal first
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest webchat and heartbeat for any remaining channel-level preservation gap.

options.title: Require surface retry parity
options.body: Queue separate webchat and heartbeat retry/requeue work regardless of the shared PR, accepting duplicated recovery policy across inbound surfaces.

options.title: Wait for more live traces
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until maintainers collect additional current-main webchat or heartbeat timing evidence before choosing the owner boundary.

recommendation.title: Review shared self-heal first
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest webchat and heartbeat for any remaining channel-level preservation gap.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits in the guarded reply-session initialization boundary where this person has recent relevant history.
